) shares are trading higher Tuesday, even as the stock remains stuck in a longer-term downtrend following the drone maker’s second-quarter earnings miss. Here’s
Red Cat Holdings stock is showing exceptional strength.
Red Cat Missed On Both Lines Last Quarter

Red Cat’s second-quarter revenue came in at $20.19 million last quarter, falling short of the $22.79 million Wall Street expected, while the company posted a loss of 26 cents a share versus an expected 22-cent loss. Despite the miss, sales still surged more than fivefold year-over-year as Red Cat pushes to become a full-spectrum autonomy provider for the military.
CEO
Jeff Thompson

credited ramped-up deliveries and expanded production, noting gross margin climbed 39 percentage points year-over-year. Red Cat ended the quarter with $325.6 million in cash and left its full-year guidance of $150 million to $180 million unchanged.

Despite today’s gain, the stock’s broader technical picture remains weak. Red Cat is trading 7.4% below its 20-day average of $8.74, 7% below its 50-day average of $8.70, and more than 26% below its 200-day average of $11.02. Given how far the stock sits under those longer benchmarks, today’s move would likely need to be treated with some skepticism rather than viewed as a genuine trend reversal, at least until the shares work their way back above those marks.
Bullish Analysts and a Tariff Tailwind May Be Driving Today’s Bounce

Part of today’s strength may reflect Wall Street’s continued optimism finally showing up in the share price. Even after falling about 57% from its 52-week high of $18.78, Red Cat still carries a consensus rating of Strong Buy to Buy, with price targets bunched between $15 and $21, well above where the stock trades today.

Coverage has been split, though: Evercore started with an Outperform call and $15 target, Needham cut its target to $15 from $20 while keeping a Buy rating, and Piper Sandler broke from the pack, launching at Neutral with just a $9 target.
Tariffs of up to 100% on foreign-made drones

last month should structurally favor a domestic maker like Red Cat, and today’s move higher may be the market finally starting to price that benefit in after weeks of the stock sliding despite the policy tailwind.
Red Cat Positions Itself As A Combat-Tested Defense Platform

Adding to the bullish backdrop, Red Cat’s own positioning and broader defense-spending trends may also be supporting the stock today. At the Piper Sandler Growth Frontiers Conference, Thompson pitched Red Cat as a defense technology company built on drones, unmanned boats and integration with military systems, Investing.com reported.

Thompson pointed to real battlefield use in Ukraine as the company’s real proof point and cited unmanned surface vehicles as a growth driver, with demand building across the Indo-Pacific, the Middle East and South America. He also flagged tougher procurement standards and skepticism from traditional Navy buyers as ongoing hurdles.

Separately, a Pentagon report this week detailed more than 30 drones lost or damaged during the ongoing Iran conflict, with total war costs estimated at $33.4 billion through June. That kind of attrition, combined with the Pentagon’s push to ramp up weapons production elsewhere, points toward sustained demand for replacement hardware.

For a domestic drone maker like Red Cat, rising defense budgets and battlefield losses could translate into new contracts, a dynamic that may be helping fuel today’s rally even though the stock’s longer-term chart has yet to reflect it.
